draft.title: Speed and acceleration
card: how fast an object moves. Speed = distance ÷ time, so 100 m covered in 20 s is 5 m/s.
speed in a stated direction. A car going 10 m/s north and one going 10 m/s south have the same speed but different velocities.
how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time taken.
Acceleration is measured in metres per second squared (m/s²). A cyclist who speeds up from 0 to 6 m/s in 3 s gains 2 m/s every second, so the acceleration is 2 m/s².
draft.remember: Speed is distance ÷ time. Acceleration is change in velocity ÷ time.

a.q: Which calculation gives the acceleration of a car?
opts: Change in velocity divided by time taken
Distance travelled divided by time taken
Change in velocity multiplied by time taken
Distance travelled multiplied by time taken
a.why: Acceleration is how quickly velocity changes, so it is the change in velocity divided by the time taken. Distance divided by time is speed, which is the most tempting mix-up.
a.clue: Acceleration is about how velocity changes.

b.q: Priya's scooter speeds up from 2 m/s to 8 m/s in 3 s along a straight path. What is its acceleration?
b.why: The change in velocity is 8 - 2 = 6 m/s. Divide by 3 s to get 2 m/s². Using 6 m/s² forgets to divide by the time.
b.clue: Subtract the starting velocity before dividing.

a.best: Change in velocity divided by time taken
